human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Review of the implemented 8094 timeline repair found a data-correctness defect: any partial-time regression is currently treated as a midnight rollover. A 3-second out-of-order event therefore gains a fabricated next-day date, and a later 00:10 event after 00:53 can be pushed to a third calendar day. Repair only this inference boundary. Ailuros may infer next-day rollover only for a large wall-clock wrap that is consistent with crossing midnight; ordinary backward jitter must remain on the carried date and surface non_monotonic_timestamp. An unanchored ambiguous partial-time event must not mutate trusted inference state.
human_pressure.why_now: Ailuros is being used as a post-run evidence analyzer. Its value depends on preserving evidence chronology without manufacturing facts. Silent date fabrication violates the existing 'never invent' normalization contract and Evidence Over Assumptions.
do_not_misread: Do not sort or reorder events to obtain monotonic timestamps.
Do not rewrite explicit full timestamps.
Do not add timezone inference, producer-specific rules, a timeline engine or a clock service.
Do not use every partial_tod < prev_tod comparison as rollover evidence.
red_lines: A small backward movement such as 10:00:05 -> 10:00:03 must never increment the calendar date.
00:53 -> 00:10 after a legitimate midnight rollover must remain on the same derived date and surface non_monotonic_timestamp.
An ambiguous partial-time event with no date anchor must not update the state used to derive later timestamps.
Explicit timestamps and input order remain untouched.

machine_core.goal: Replace the over-broad partial-time rollover rule with a conservative deterministic boundary so Ailuros derives next-day dates only for a genuine wall-clock wrap and reports ordinary backward jitter instead of silently fabricating dates.
invariants: Explicit datetime timestamps are preserved exactly.
Input event order is preserved exactly.
A partial-time backward jump of 12 hours or less is not a rollover; it remains on the carried date and is eligible for non_monotonic_timestamp reporting.
A backward jump greater than 12 hours is the only partial-time wall-clock wrap this MVP may treat as deterministic midnight rollover.
An exact 12-hour backward jump remains ambiguous/non-monotonic rather than being promoted to rollover.
Unanchored partial-time evidence never mutates trusted date/time inference state.
No producer/source label affects temporal inference.

producer.artifact: ordered normalized events containing explicit timestamps and/or partial_time

observable_effect.assertion: Only a backward partial-time wall-clock jump greater than 12 hours increments the carried calendar date; smaller/equal backward movements retain the carried date and surface chronology regression instead of fabricating a later day.

proofs.assertion: 10:00:05 -> 10:00:03 does not increment date and produces non_monotonic_timestamp.
23:53 -> 00:53 -> 00:10 yields dates Jan 1, Jan 2, Jan 2; the last event is non-monotonic and never Jan 3.
A partial-time event before any explicit date is reported ambiguous and cannot influence inference after a later explicit anchor.
Explicit full timestamps remain unchanged even when non-monotonic.

failure_semantics: Ordinary backward partial-time movement is evidence disorder, not proof of a new calendar day.
Ambiguous no-anchor partial time remains ambiguous and does not become trusted state.
Temporal regression does not imply execution failure, root cause or producer defect.

steps.title: Characterize the false rollover cases
details: Assert exact derived dates and regression reasons, not only list length.

steps.title: Narrow the rollover predicate
details: Replace the generic partial_tod < prev_tod rollover condition with the smallest local predicate that treats only a backward wall-clock jump greater than 12 hours as midnight rollover.
Do not introduce a configurable heuristic framework.

steps.title: Stop ambiguous events from poisoning trusted state
details: When carried_date is absent, keep timestamp=None and emit ambiguous_partial_time_no_anchor as today, but do not update prev_tod/prev_dt/carried state from that event.

steps.title: Lock temporal invariants
details: Retain existing legitimate rollover, explicit timestamp preservation and input-order tests.
Add exact-12-hour boundary coverage so it remains non-rollover.

acceptance: 23:53 -> 00:53 still rolls to the next date.
10:00:05 -> 10:00:03 stays on the same date and emits non_monotonic_timestamp.
23:53 -> 00:53 -> 00:10 never fabricates a third day; the last event stays on the second day and emits non_monotonic_timestamp.
Unanchored partial-time evidence emits ambiguity but does not affect later anchored derivation.
Explicit timestamps and event order are unchanged.
ruff, mypy, focused tests and the full pytest suite pass.

must_check: The implementation no longer treats every partial-time regression as midnight rollover.
The greater-than-12-hours rollover boundary is implemented exactly; an equal-or-smaller backward jump does not increment the date.
The two concrete review regressions produce non_monotonic_timestamp without date fabrication.
Ambiguous no-anchor partial-time evidence cannot mutate trusted inference state.
Explicit timestamps and event order remain unchanged.
No producer-specific or generalized temporal subsystem is introduced.
Focused tests, full pytest, ruff and mypy pass.
reject_if: 10:00:05 -> 10:00:03 is assigned to the next day.
An ambiguous no-anchor event changes later date inference.
Events are reordered or explicit timestamps rewritten.
The implementation adds a timeline engine, configurable heuristic framework, timezone inference or producer-specific branch.
Validation fails or forbidden files change.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: False rollover prevention, ambiguous-state isolation and legitimate midnight rollover preservation.
